key_insight: InfantNet provides a large infant-specific benchmark that improves pose and body-shape estimation over direct transfer of adult-trained models.
clinical_relevance: The dataset could support research in developmental monitoring and infant movement analysis, but clinical utility is not established in the abstract.
method: Collect 108,902 RGB images of infants aged 6–18 months and annotate 2D keypoints.
Add 3D pose and shape labels with full SMIL parameters for 11,642 images.
Use iterative annotation, multi-view rendering, and reprojection-error filtering to refine labels.
evidence_signal: Benchmark experiments report consistent gains after infant-specific fine-tuning, especially for 3D estimation, but the abstract provides no numerical performance metrics.
watch_item: Performance outside the 6–18-month age range and in clinical settings remains unestablished.
paper_title: InfantNet: A Large Scale Dataset for Infant Body Pose and Shape Estimation
